title: Your first week in Türkiye
question: What should I do in my first week?
summary: Get a Turkish number, register at your university, then start your tax number and residence permit. Each step usually takes one visit.

intro.heading: Start with the steps that have deadlines
intro.body: Some steps have legal deadlines, others just make daily life easier. Follow this order and your first week stays calm.
intro.tip: Carry your passport for every official step, even if you entered Türkiye with your ID card.

sections.heading: Day 1-2: Get connected
sections.body: Many university and government systems ask for a Turkish phone number.
items: Get a Turkish SIM at an official operator store; airport shops are usually more expensive
Save your address exactly as it is written in Turkish
Follow your local ESN section and ask for an ESN buddy

sections.heading: Day 2-4: University
sections.body: Your university's international office knows the local process best. Visit them early.
sections.tip: University systems are often busy in the first weeks. If something fails, try again later; it usually works.
items: Register at the international office with your passport, a photo and your Turkish number
Collect your student certificate (öğrenci belgesi)
Bring any arrival forms your home university needs signed
Join your university's orientation day to meet other exchange students

sections.heading: Day 3-7: Paperwork and settling in
sections.body: Start the residence permit now; appointments fill up fast in September, October and February.
items: Get your free tax number
Arrange health insurance that covers your whole stay
Start your residence permit application on e-ikamet
Get a transport card for your city

offers.label: ESNcard
offers.title: Get your ESNcard
offers.description: Your ESN membership card. It gives you access to ESN events and discounts from local, national and international partners. Buy it from your local ESN section.

title: Residence permit (ikamet)
question: Do I need a residence permit and how do I get one?
summary: Staying longer than 90 days? You need a student residence permit, even with a visa. Apply in your first month, ideally your first week.

intro.heading: Count your days from arrival
intro.body: EU citizens can stay 90 days in any 180-day period. Leaving and coming back does not reset the count. Other students can stay as long as their visa allows.
intro.tip: You can stay legally while your application is processed. Don't wait to start.

sections.heading: Do I need one?
sections.body: Most Erasmus students do, because a semester is longer than 90 days.
items: Staying less than 90 days: you do not need a permit
Staying longer than 90 days: apply, even if you have a visa
Turkish ID or Blue Card (Mavi Kart) holders: you do not need to apply

sections.heading: Documents to prepare
sections.body: Prepare everything before you fill in the online form.
items: Passport, plus copies of the photo page and your latest entry stamp
4 printed biometric photos from the last 6 months, plus the same photo in digital form
Student certificate from your university
Health insurance that covers your whole stay
Proof of address: notarized rental contract, dorm document or e-Devlet address record
Tax number and the fee payment receipt
An active Turkish phone number

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.body: Your international office tells you which steps they handle for you.
sections.tip: Use the Turkish version of e-ikamet with your browser's translator. Switching the language can break the form.
items: Fill in the form at e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr in one sitting; saving progress is unreliable
Download the form as a PDF and print it
Pay the fee shown on your application
Give your fingerprints at the migration office; go early in the morning
Submit your documents to your university or the migration office

sections.heading: While you wait
sections.body: Cards usually arrive in about four weeks, but it can take longer in autumn. Track the status on e-ikamet.
items: You can travel within Türkiye
To leave and come back, carry your application confirmation and approval letter
Once you have the card, never let it expire while you are abroad

sections.heading: Staying another semester?
sections.body: Apply for an extension on e-ikamet before your permit expires.
items: Bring a new student certificate, new insurance and current proof of address
Register for electronic notifications (UETS) at a PTT post office after your first card; renewals need it

sections.heading: Need help?
sections.body: You are not the first to do this.
items: Call YIMER on 157, the foreigners' helpline
Ask your university's international office
Ask your local ESN section; they help students with this every semester

offers.label: ESN Türkiye partner
offers.title: Health insurance for your permit
offers.description: Gulf Insurance offers health insurance for Erasmus students through its partnership with ESN Türkiye. You can create your policy online.

title: Phone, SIM and eSIM
question: Will my phone work in Türkiye?
summary: Two different limits apply. A SIM bought with your passport works for about 3 months. A phone bought abroad works for about 120 days, then needs a costly registration.

intro.heading: Your SIM and your phone are separate topics
intro.body: The SIM limit is about your line. The phone limit is about your device's IMEI number. Plan for both from your first week.
intro.tip: Dial *#06# to see your phone's IMEI number.

sections.heading: Getting a Turkish SIM
sections.body: Turkcell, Vodafone and Türk Telekom sell prepaid SIM cards. Bimcell and Pttcell are smaller brands on Türk Telekom's network.
items: Bring your passport to an official operator store
You pay for the SIM and the first month, then top up every month
Compare packages; prices differ between operators

sections.heading: Keeping your number after 3 months
sections.body: A SIM registered with your passport works for about 3 months.
items: To keep it longer, show your residence permit card at your operator's store
An acceptance letter is not enough to extend the line

sections.heading: Your phone after 120 days
sections.body: A phone bought abroad must be registered to keep working on Turkish networks. The fee is ₺54,258 in 2026.
sections.tip: Start early. The registration period can vary and the process can take a few days.
items: Register: pay the fee at a tax office, then register at your operator or on e-Devlet
Bring your phone, passport with a clear entry stamp and residence permit
Or buy a simple phone in Türkiye; it works without registration
Or use your own phone on Wi-Fi only

title: Health insurance and healthcare
question: What do I do if I get sick?
summary: Keep valid health insurance for your whole stay; your residence permit depends on it. In an emergency, call 112. For small problems, start at a pharmacy.

intro.heading: Insurance first, then everything else
intro.body: Your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) does not work in Türkiye. You need insurance that is valid here.
intro.tip: Save 112 in your phone. One number covers ambulance, police and fire.

sections.heading: Your insurance options
sections.body: Both options are accepted for the residence permit. Insurance that ends before your stay does is a common reason for delays.
items: Private health insurance from a company in Türkiye, covering your whole stay
General Health Insurance (GSS) from SGK, the state social security agency
For GSS, apply within 3 months of your enrollment; you cannot join later

sections.heading: When you feel sick
sections.body: Pharmacists in Türkiye give advice and sell many medicines without a prescription.
items: Go to a pharmacy (eczane) for small problems
At night, find the on-duty pharmacy (nöbetçi eczane); the list is on every pharmacy door
For an appointment, use your university's health centre or a hospital
Bring your passport and insurance details to every visit

offers.label: ESN Türkiye partner
offers.title: Gulf Insurance for Erasmus students
offers.description: Health insurance designed for incoming Erasmus students, valid for the residence permit. Buy and manage your policy online.

title: Money, banks and tax number
question: Do I need a tax number or a Turkish bank account?
summary: Get a tax number early; you need it for your residence permit, a bank account or a rental contract. Cards work almost everywhere, but carry some cash.

intro.heading: Start with your tax number
intro.body: A tax number (vergi kimlik numarası) is an ID number for official and financial tasks. It does not mean you pay tax.
intro.tip: Enter your name exactly as it is written in your passport.

sections.heading: Get your tax number
sections.body: You only need your passport and an address in Türkiye.
items: Apply online on the Revenue Administration's foreigners page at dijital.gib.gov.tr
Or go to any tax office (vergi dairesi) with your passport
Download or keep the document; you will need it for your residence permit

sections.heading: Paying day to day
sections.body: Contactless cards are accepted in most shops, cafés and restaurants.
sections.tip: When a card machine or ATM asks, choose to pay in Turkish lira (₺). Paying in your home currency usually costs more.
items: Carry some cash for markets, small shops and dolmuş minibuses
Use ATMs of large banks inside branches or malls
Turn on international payments for your foreign card before you arrive

sections.heading: Opening a Turkish bank account
sections.body: For one semester, your home card is often enough. If you need a local account, requirements differ by bank.
items: Bring your passport, tax number and student certificate
Some banks also ask for your residence permit
Ask your international office which banks students use

title: Finding a place to live
question: How do I find safe housing?
summary: See the place before you sign or pay. Make sure the landlord gives you a contract you can register; you need it for your residence permit.

intro.heading: Your address decides your residence permit
intro.body: You cannot get a residence permit without a registered address. Sort out proper housing early.
intro.tip: Not sure if a listing is real? Send it to your ESN buddy or local ESN section. They can tell you if it looks reliable.

sections.heading: Where students look
sections.body: Most exchange students choose a private dorm or a shared flat.
items: Student housing groups on social media
Students who are leaving at the end of the semester
Private dorms near your campus

sections.heading: Before you pay
sections.body: Take your time; a good room is worth a few extra days in a hostel.
items: Do not sign or pay before you see the place, or at least confirm it is real
Get a receipt for every payment, including the deposit
Check which bills are included: electricity, water, gas, internet and building fee (aidat)

sections.heading: A contract that works for your permit
sections.body: Ask about this before you agree on the flat.
items: The contract usually needs to be in Turkish; English-only contracts are often not accepted
It must be notarized; the landlord usually comes to the notary with proof of ownership
Living in a dorm? Ask for a dorm document showing your address

title: Getting around like a local
question: How do I use public transport in my city?
summary: Each city has its own transport card. In Istanbul, a student Istanbulkart gives you lower fares on almost all public transport. Get it right after your university registration.

intro.heading: One card per city
intro.body: Buy a card at a station machine or kiosk, top it up and tap it when you board. Google Maps and Moovit show routes and times.
intro.tip: In Istanbul, take a ferry at least once. A tea or simit on the deck is one of the nicest ways to see the city.

sections.heading: Istanbul: student Istanbulkart
sections.body: Works on metro, tram, Marmaray, metrobüs, buses and city ferries. As of August 2026, a student journey costs ₺22.55 and a monthly student pass (abonman) ₺653.
sections.tip: At the centre you can say: "Pasaportumla öğrenci Istanbulkartı çıkarmak istiyorum." (I'd like a student Istanbulkart with my passport.)
items: Apply in person at an Istanbulkart application centre; this is easiest for new arrivals
Bring your passport, a recent photo, a student certificate from the last month and your temporary YÖK number
Pay the card fee (₺140 as of August 2026)
Use the Istanbulkart Mobil app to top up, load a monthly pass and pay by QR
Problems with your application? Call ALO 153

sections.heading: Ankara and Izmir
sections.body: Ankara uses AnkaraKart and Izmir uses Izmirim Kart. Student discount rules for exchange students differ by city.
items: Buy a standard card at a station on your first day
Ask your international office whether you can get a student card

sections.heading: Taxis
sections.body: Taxis run on a meter. Ride-hailing apps such as BiTaksi and Uber work in big cities.
items: Ask the driver to start the meter (taksimetre)
Use an app if you want a record of your trip
Keep small notes for short rides

title: Travelling around Türkiye
question: How do I travel between cities?
summary: Fly for long distances, take the high-speed train between connected cities and use coaches for almost everywhere else. Book popular routes early.

intro.heading: Pick by distance, budget and time
intro.body: Türkiye is large. Plane, train, coach and ferry each have their best use.
intro.tip: Prices change a lot by date. Compare early and check ESNcard discounts before you book.

sections.heading: By plane
sections.body: Fastest for long trips, such as to Antalya, Trabzon or eastern Türkiye.
items: Main domestic airlines: Turkish Airlines, Pegasus and AJet
Compare departure airports in big cities; prices can differ

sections.heading: By train
sections.body: High-speed trains (YHT) are comfortable and avoid airport transfers. Buy tickets on the TCDD website or app.
items: Book weekend high-speed trains early; they sell out
For the Eastern Express (Doğu Ekspresi), check when tickets are released and plan well ahead

sections.heading: By coach
sections.body: Intercity coaches reach places that trains and planes do not.
items: Pamukkale and Kamil Koç are reliable, comfortable companies
Compare companies and times on Obilet
Using a company you don't know? Read reviews before you book
Many companies run free shuttles (servis) to their terminals

sections.heading: By ferry
sections.body: Sea buses connect cities around the Sea of Marmara, such as Istanbul, Yalova, Bursa and Bandırma.
items: Check IDO and BUDO for routes and tickets
Schedules change with season and weather; check before you go

offers.label: ESNcard
offers.title: Kamil Koç and FlixBus discounts
offers.description: ESNcard holders can get discounts on Kamil Koç and FlixBus coaches. Check the current offer before you book.

offers.label: ESNcard
offers.title: Ryanair discounts
offers.description: ESNcard holders get discounts on Ryanair flights and extra checked luggage. Check the current terms before you book.

title: Museums, culture and events
question: How can I visit museums for less?
summary: As a student enrolled in Türkiye, you can get a discounted museum card for one year. It covers more than 350 museums and archaeological sites.

intro.heading: Get your MüzeKart early
intro.body: You will probably use it more than you expect, in your city and while travelling around Türkiye.
intro.tip: You can visit each museum or site up to twice a year with the card.

sections.heading: Discounted MüzeKart (MüzeKart Indirimli)
sections.body: Valid for one year at state museums, National Palaces and the Çanakkale historic sites. As of August 2026, it costs ₺100.
items: Bring your passport or another photo ID
Bring your student ID or a student certificate
Buy it at an official museum ticket office; the list is on muze.gov.tr

sections.heading: Concerts, theatre and events
sections.body: There is almost always something happening in big cities.
items: Check Biletix and Biletinial for events and tickets
Follow your local ESN section for trips, culture nights and parties with other students

sections.heading: Learn some Turkish
sections.body: Even a few words make daily life easier and locals appreciate it.
items: Ask your university about Turkish courses for exchange students
Join tandem or language exchange events
